title: Get screw-cap media bottles ready for the autoclave: caps loosened but left on, bottles in a rimmed tray
instruction: Get these bottles ready for the autoclave.
context: Lab technicians and sterile-processing staff autoclave liquid media every day, following a rule they learn in training and are not told each time (O*NET 19-4021.00, Biological Technicians; 31-9093.00, Medical Equipment Preparers). University biosafety and autoclave procedures all give it for liquids in screw-cap bottles: loosen each cap about a quarter to a half turn, but leave it on. A tight cap traps the steam pressure, and the bottle can crack or burst in the chamber or when it is opened. A cap taken off lets the medium boil over and leaves it open to contamination when it comes out. In the autoclave the bottles stand in a tray with a raised rim, which catches anything that boils over or breaks. Here three bottles of freshly made media stand on the bench beside an empty tray, with their caps done up snug as they were after mixing.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. An empty polypropylene autoclave tray, light gray, is fixed on the bench, centered at x 33, y 0: 14 cm deep (x 26 to 40), 36 cm wide (y -18 to 18), with a rim 3.5 cm tall and 0.6 cm thick and a 0.4 cm floor. Three 50 mL borosilicate glass media bottles stand upright on the bench, each 4.6 cm across with a shoulder and neck, 8.4 cm tall to the pouring ring and 10.4 cm with its cap, 120 g with its liquid. They hold 50 mL of amber nutrient broth at x 22, y 24; pale yellow buffered saline at x 25, y -24; and pink cell-culture medium at x 34, y 25. Each has a white label with a strip of autoclave tape on its left side. Each bottle has a blue GL 32 polypropylene screw cap, 3.7 cm across and 2 cm tall, with a white marker line across its top. The thread is right-handed (loosens counterclockwise seen from above), rises 4 mm per turn, and comes off 1.25 turns back from the seat. Every cap starts snug: screwed down to its seat and 20 degrees past it.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole run. Each cap's angle is measured from its seat, the point where it first bottoms out on the bottle. A cap counts as loosened when it is at least 45 degrees back from the seat, still on its thread, and at least 45 degrees of that turning was done with a gripper holding it: fingers closed on the cap to its width (an empty closed hand does not count), with the tool point within 1.5 cm of the cap's axis and middle. Two mistakes score 0 and are irreversible: any cap coming off its thread (more than 1.25 turns back) at any point, even if it is screwed back on; and any bottle tipping past 45 degrees for 2 control steps. The score is also 0 if any cap ends not loosened, since that bottle can burst. With every cap loosened: 0.25 if any cap is more than 270 degrees back, on by less than half a turn of thread. Otherwise 0.5 unless every bottle stands upright (within 15 degrees) and still (moving under 2 cm/s) on the tray floor, with its base wholly inside the rim and no gripper holding it (fingers under 60 % open with the tool point within 2 cm of the bottle or cap). Then 1.0 with both arms back home and still, or 0.9 if not. The arms count as home with each tool point within 3 cm of where it started, because they are put back so the workspace is clear for the next person or job. Success is a full score held for 1 s. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.9, 1.0. In a real trial, mark each cap and bottle with a vertical line before the trial. Afterwards read each cap's turn against its bottle's line with a printed protractor ring, check by hand that each cap still turns at least half a turn before it lifts off, and photograph the tray from above. Watch the video for a cap coming off or a bottle tipping.
reset_notes: Screw each cap back on until it seats, then snug it a little further (20 degrees in the simulation), and set the bottles back on their taped spots on the bench. Nothing is used up.
fidelity: True size. The thread is modeled: each cap rides a slide and hinge driven to 4 mm of rise per turn, with a small resisting torque and a stop 60 degrees past the seat. No flanks or liner, and the break-loose torque is far below a real cap's. A cap past 1.25 turns counts as off but stays on the bottle's axis. No steam or heat. The tray is fixed. The liquids are solid and do not slosh.
